normalization_or_editorial_flags.issue: cette nuit and tonight overlap but can differ from ce soir; choose time-of-day translations consistently for standalone learner pairs.
planter quelqu'un is colloquial for ditch/leave stranded; valid but register-marked relative to the workbook's standard-formal variants.
qui c'est is conversational French; decide whether to retain colloquial variants alongside standard qui il est.
faire se sentir constructions are calqued/heavy; native editorial review should rewrite into idiomatic contemporary French.
The French asks whether/how the listener can help rather than mirroring the English existential 'Is there anything you can do to help?'; semantically close but structurally awkward.
Mood choices with vouloir after indefinite/interrogative antecedents vary; native editorial review should normalize without treating legitimate subjunctive forms as errors.
ici maps to here, while English 'over here' adds a deictic nuance; acceptable but not exact.
je vous en prie means 'please/go ahead' in context; English 'here you are' implies physically handing over the dictionary. Review if exact situational equivalence is required.
je te/vous prie is formal/dated compared with surrounding contemporary prompts; standardize politeness register.
English explicitly includes here; French omits it. Not necessarily contradictory, but the standalone pair is not exact.
dire un mot is literally 'say a word'; avoir un mot/te parler un instant would more directly match English 'have a word with you'.
French asks whether the speaker can do anything else; English asks whether there is anything else the listener wants done. Close but not fully equivalent.
c'est quoi que is strongly conversational; keep only if colloquial French is intentionally within scope.
là maintenant is awkward/calqued; prefer tout de suite or maintenant for standard learner French.
